questions.prompt: The ability to maintain the internal environment constant is called ____.
questions.explanation: The ability to maintain the internal environment constant is called homeostasis.

questions.prompt: Osmoregulation, excretion and thermoregulation are all parts of ____.
questions.explanation: Osmoregulation, excretion and thermoregulation are all parts of homeostasis.

questions.prompt: Body fluids are important components of the ____ environment.
questions.explanation: Body fluids are important components of the internal environment.

questions.prompt: Along with water and solutes, the component of the internal environment readily affected by the external environment is ____.
questions.explanation: Along with water and solutes, the component of the internal environment readily affected by the external environment is temperature.

questions.prompt: The process by which the amount of water and solutes is maintained in the body is called ____.
questions.explanation: The process by which the amount of water and solutes is maintained in the body is called osmoregulation.

questions.prompt: The maintenance of the internal body temperature within a tolerable range is called ____.
questions.explanation: The maintenance of the internal body temperature within a tolerable range is called thermoregulation.

questions.prompt: A desert plant with deep roots, very few stomata and a thick waxy cuticle is a:
questions.explanation: Xerophytes live in dry environments and have deep roots, very few stomata and a thick waxy cuticle.

questions.prompt: A water lily growing in a pond belongs to which group of plants?
questions.explanation: Water lilies are the most common example of hydrophytes.

questions.prompt: The four groups of plants are mesophytes, hydrophytes, xerophytes and ____.
questions.explanation: The four groups of plants are mesophytes, hydrophytes, xerophytes and halophytes.

questions.prompt: A plant living in a salty marsh that excretes extra salt through salt glands on its leaves is a:
questions.explanation: Halophytes live in salty waters and excrete excess salt from salt glands on the leaves.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT an adaptation of xerophytes?
questions.explanation: Xerophytes have very few stomata, a thick waxy cuticle, deep roots and succulent organs.

questions.prompt: Which plants control extra transpiration by closing their stomata in a shortage of water?
questions.explanation: Mesophytes close their stomata when they face a shortage of water.

questions.prompt: Which pair of plant and group is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Cacti are xerophytes; water lilies are hydrophytes, sea grasses are halophytes and maize is a mesophyte.

questions.prompt: Hydrophytes and halophytes both live in water. How do their problems differ?
questions.explanation: Freshwater hydrophytes have extra water entering them, whereas halophytes tend to lose water to the salty environment.

options: Hydrophytes absorb salts by active transport, while halophytes remove water through stomata
Both groups remove extra water through the cuticle
Both groups store water in succulent stems
Hydrophytes remove extra water entering their bodies, while halophytes absorb salts so water does not leave their cells

questions.prompt: In the word hydrophyte, hydro means ____ and phyte means plant.
questions.explanation: In the word hydrophyte, hydro means water and phyte means plant.

questions.prompt: In the word xerophyte, xero means ____ and phyte means plant.
questions.explanation: In the word xerophyte, xero means dry and phyte means plant.

questions.prompt: In the word halophyte, halo means ____ and phyte means plant.
questions.explanation: In the word halophyte, halo means salt and phyte means plant.

questions.prompt: Mesophytes are the terrestrial plants which live where a sufficient quantity of ____ is available.
questions.explanation: Mesophytes are the terrestrial plants which live where a sufficient quantity of water is available.

questions.prompt: Mesophytes absorb water through their ____.
questions.explanation: Mesophytes absorb water through their roots.

questions.prompt: Maize (corn), clover and rose are examples of ____.
questions.explanation: Maize (corn), clover and rose are examples of mesophytes.

questions.prompt: In a sufficient supply of water, mesophytes keep their stomata ____ to promote the loss of excess water.
questions.explanation: In a sufficient supply of water, mesophytes keep their stomata open to promote the loss of excess water.

questions.prompt: Most of the body surface of mesophytes is covered with a ____, which prevents water loss.
questions.explanation: Most of the body surface of mesophytes is covered with a waxy cuticle, which prevents water loss.

questions.prompt: Hydrophytes are the plants which live in freshwater or in ____.
questions.explanation: Hydrophytes are the plants which live in freshwater or in wet soil.

questions.prompt: The most common example of hydrophytes is the ____.
questions.explanation: The most common example of hydrophytes is the water lily.

questions.prompt: Water keeps on entering the bodies of hydrophytes through their whole ____.
questions.explanation: Water keeps on entering the bodies of hydrophytes through their whole surface.

questions.prompt: Many hydrophytes have ____ leaves that float on the surface of the water.
questions.explanation: Many hydrophytes have broad leaves that float on the surface of the water.

questions.prompt: The floating leaves of hydrophytes have a large number of stomata on their ____ surface.
questions.explanation: The floating leaves of hydrophytes have a large number of stomata on their upper surface.

questions.prompt: Water moves out of hydrophytes through the ____ of their floating leaves.
questions.explanation: Water moves out of hydrophytes through the stomata of their floating leaves.

questions.prompt: Xerophytes live in ____ environments such as deserts.
questions.explanation: Xerophytes live in dry environments such as deserts.

questions.prompt: Xerophytes have ____ roots to absorb water from almost dry soil.
questions.explanation: Xerophytes have deep roots to absorb water from almost dry soil.

questions.prompt: The body surface of xerophytes has very ____ stomata.
questions.explanation: The body surface of xerophytes has very few stomata.

questions.prompt: The body surface of xerophytes is covered with thick ____ cuticles to reduce the loss of water.
questions.explanation: The body surface of xerophytes is covered with thick waxy cuticles to reduce the loss of water.

questions.prompt: Some xerophytes, e.g. cacti, store water in soft and juicy stems or roots called ____ organs.
questions.explanation: Some xerophytes, e.g. cacti, store water in soft and juicy stems or roots called succulent organs.

questions.prompt: Halophytes live in habitats with ____ waters, such as the sea or salty marshes.
questions.explanation: Halophytes live in habitats with salty waters, such as the sea or salty marshes.

questions.prompt: The sea and salty marshes are the habitat of ____.
questions.explanation: The sea and salty marshes are the habitat of halophytes.

questions.prompt: Many ____ are halophytes.
questions.explanation: Many sea grasses are halophytes.

questions.prompt: The bodies of halophytes have ____ salt concentration than the external environment.
questions.explanation: The bodies of halophytes have less salt concentration than the external environment.

questions.prompt: Because halophytes absorb salts by active transport, ____ does not move out of their cells.
questions.explanation: Because halophytes absorb salts by active transport, water does not move out of their cells.

questions.prompt: Plants do not possess any special ____ for excretion.
questions.explanation: Plants do not possess any special organs for excretion.

questions.prompt: Plants need to excrete carbon dioxide, oxygen, water, latex, resins and ____.
questions.explanation: Plants need to excrete carbon dioxide, oxygen, water, latex, resins and gums.

questions.prompt: Which process removes extra water from the leaves of grasses at night?
questions.explanation: Transpiration does not occur at night, so grasses use guttation through pores at the tips or edges of leaves.

questions.prompt: Which gas is excreted through the open stomata of plants at night?
questions.explanation: At night there is no photosynthesis, so carbon dioxide is excreted through the open stomata.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly differentiates transpiration from guttation?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is loss of water as vapours; guttation is loss of water as little drops through pores at the tips or edges of leaves.

options: Transpiration loses water as drops at night, while guttation loses it as vapours by day
Both occur only through the lenticels
Transpiration loses water as vapours, mostly by day, while guttation loses it as drops at night

questions.prompt: During the day, carbon dioxide is retained in the leaves and used for ____.
questions.explanation: During the day, carbon dioxide is retained in the leaves and used for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: At night, when there is no photosynthesis, carbon dioxide is excreted through the open ____ of the leaves.
questions.explanation: At night, when there is no photosynthesis, carbon dioxide is excreted through the open stomata of the leaves.

questions.prompt: The extra oxygen produced during photosynthesis is released out through the ____.
questions.explanation: The extra oxygen produced during photosynthesis is released out through the stomata.

questions.prompt: Plants store large amounts of water in the ____ of their cells.
questions.explanation: Plants store large amounts of water in the vacuoles of their cells.

questions.prompt: Water stored in vacuoles results in ____, which provides support to the soft parts of the plant.
questions.explanation: Water stored in vacuoles results in turgor, which provides support to the soft parts of the plant.

questions.prompt: Turgor provides support to the ____ parts of the plant body.
questions.explanation: Turgor provides support to the soft parts of the plant body.

questions.prompt: ____ is the loss of water from the plant surface in the form of vapours.
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant surface in the form of vapours.

questions.prompt: There are ____ types of transpiration.
questions.explanation: There are three types of transpiration.

questions.prompt: Plants remove their extra water by transpiration during the ____.
questions.explanation: Plants remove their extra water by transpiration during the day.

questions.prompt: Transpiration through the stomata is called ____ transpiration.
questions.explanation: Transpiration through the stomata is called stomatal transpiration.

questions.prompt: Transpiration through the cuticle is called ____ transpiration.
questions.explanation: Transpiration through the cuticle is called cuticular transpiration.

questions.prompt: Transpiration through the lenticels is called ____ transpiration.
questions.explanation: Transpiration through the lenticels is called lenticular transpiration.

questions.prompt: Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant surface in the form of ____.
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant surface in the form of vapours.

questions.prompt: ____ is the removal of extra water as little drops through pores at the tips or edges of leaves.
questions.explanation: Guttation is the removal of extra water as little drops through pores at the tips or edges of leaves.

questions.prompt: Water is lost as vapours in transpiration but as little ____ in guttation.
questions.explanation: Water is lost as vapours in transpiration but as little drops in guttation.

questions.prompt: The ____ plant excretes latex.
questions.explanation: The rubber plant excretes latex.

questions.prompt: The Acacia tree excretes ____.
questions.explanation: The Acacia tree excretes gums.

questions.prompt: Coniferous trees excrete ____.
questions.explanation: Coniferous trees excrete resins.

questions.prompt: Some plants store wastes in their stems, leaves or roots in the form of harmless ____.
questions.explanation: Some plants store wastes in their stems, leaves or roots in the form of harmless crystals.

questions.prompt: Some plants store wastes in their leaves, and the wastes are lost when the leaves ____.
questions.explanation: Some plants store wastes in their leaves, and the wastes are lost when the leaves fall.

questions.prompt: Some plants excrete their wastes through special ____ by applying force.
questions.explanation: Some plants excrete their wastes through special pores by applying force.

questions.prompt: The plant excreting gums is the ____ tree.
questions.explanation: The plant excreting gums is the Acacia tree.

questions.prompt: The plants excreting resins are the ____ trees.
questions.explanation: The plants excreting resins are the coniferous trees.

questions.prompt: Resins, gums and latex are economically very important and are used in many ____ products.
questions.explanation: Resins, gums and latex are economically very important and are used in many industrial products.

questions.prompt: The plant excreting mucilage is the ____.
questions.explanation: The plant excreting mucilage is the ladyfinger.

questions.prompt: Fig. 11.4 shows the three types of ____ in a tree.
questions.explanation: Fig. 11.4 shows the three types of transpiration in a tree.

questions.prompt: Water drops coming out from the margins of leaves in Fig. 11.5 show ____.
questions.explanation: Water drops coming out from the margins of leaves in Fig. 11.5 show guttation.

questions.prompt: In human beings the main organs involved in homeostasis are the skin, lungs and ____.
questions.explanation: In human beings the main organs involved in homeostasis are the skin, lungs and kidneys.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the main organs of homeostasis in human beings?
questions.explanation: The main organs of homeostasis are the skin, lungs and kidneys.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a part of homeostasis?
questions.explanation: Osmoregulation, excretion and thermoregulation are the parts of homeostasis described in the chapter.

questions.prompt: Along with energy, cellular respiration produces water and ____ in every cell.
questions.explanation: Along with energy, cellular respiration produces water and carbon dioxide in every cell.

questions.prompt: Blood transports carbon dioxide from the cells to the ____.
questions.explanation: Blood transports carbon dioxide from the cells to the lungs.

questions.prompt: The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the body when the air is ____.
questions.explanation: The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the body when the air is exhaled.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide is an ____ gas.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is an acidic gas.

questions.prompt: The accumulation of carbon dioxide can make the blood and other body tissues more ____.
questions.explanation: The accumulation of carbon dioxide can make the blood and other body tissues more acidic.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air in the alveoli by ____.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air in the alveoli by diffusion.

questions.prompt: The lungs act as homeostatic organs by keeping the ____ concentration down to a certain level.
questions.explanation: The lungs act as homeostatic organs by keeping the carbon dioxide concentration down to a certain level.

questions.prompt: Which organ removes carbon dioxide from the blood into the exhaled air?
questions.explanation: CO₂ diffuses from the blood into the air in the alveoli and is exhaled.

questions.prompt: The skin of human beings and other mammals has been adapted as the organ of ____.
questions.explanation: The skin of human beings and other mammals has been adapted as the organ of thermoregulation.

questions.prompt: The skin is the organ of thermoregulation in humans and other ____.
questions.explanation: The skin is the organ of thermoregulation in humans and other mammals.

questions.prompt: In cold conditions, goose bumps are formed because the:
questions.explanation: The muscles at the base of the hair contract, the hairs stand up and goose bumps form.

options: Muscles at the base of the hair contract

questions.prompt: Which statement about the skin in warm conditions is correct?
questions.explanation: In warm conditions, sweat glands produce sweat and the evaporation of sweat cools the body.

options: Sweat evaporates and excess body heat escapes
Hairs stand up to trap warm air
Goose bumps form a blanket of warm air
Muscles at the base of the hair contract

questions.prompt: When the muscles at the base of the hair contract, the hairs ____.
questions.explanation: When the muscles at the base of the hair contract, the hairs stand up.

questions.prompt: In cold conditions, hair and goose bumps make a blanket of ____.
questions.explanation: In cold conditions, hair and goose bumps make a blanket of warm air.

questions.prompt: In cold conditions, the muscles attached at the base of the ____ contract.
questions.explanation: In cold conditions, the muscles attached at the base of the hair contract.

questions.prompt: In cold conditions, the muscles at the base of the hair ____.
questions.explanation: In cold conditions, the muscles at the base of the hair contract.

questions.prompt: In warm conditions, the skin provides a cooling effect when ____ is produced.
questions.explanation: In warm conditions, the skin provides a cooling effect when sweat is produced.

questions.prompt: Excess body heat escapes through the ____ of sweat.
questions.explanation: Excess body heat escapes through the evaporation of sweat.

questions.prompt: Sweat removes some extra water, salts and ____ from the body.
questions.explanation: Sweat removes some extra water, salts and nitrogenous wastes from the body.

questions.prompt: The removal of urea in sweat makes the skin also an ____ organ.
questions.explanation: The removal of urea in sweat makes the skin also an excretory organ.

questions.prompt: Dogs keep their tongue hanging outside the mouth because they have ____ sweat glands in their skin.
questions.explanation: Dogs keep their tongue hanging outside the mouth because they have fewer sweat glands in their skin.

questions.prompt: A hanging tongue increases the ____ of water in dogs, which produces a cooling effect.
questions.explanation: A hanging tongue increases the evaporation of water in dogs, which produces a cooling effect.

questions.prompt: The normal set point of the hypothalamus is ____ °C.
questions.explanation: The normal set point of the hypothalamus is 37 °C.

questions.prompt: In bacterial and viral infections, the number of ____ increases.
questions.explanation: In bacterial and viral infections, the number of leukocytes increases.

questions.prompt: In fever, the set point of the ____ of the brain is displaced above the normal point.
questions.explanation: In fever, the set point of the hypothalamus of the brain is displaced above the normal point.

questions.prompt: In fever, the brain sends messages to body parts to produce ____.
questions.explanation: In fever, the brain sends messages to body parts to produce heat.

questions.prompt: Fever helps in stimulating the protective mechanisms against ____.
questions.explanation: Fever helps in stimulating the protective mechanisms against pathogens.

questions.prompt: The ____ are the most important organs of homeostasis in human beings and other animals.
questions.explanation: The kidneys are the most important organs of homeostasis in human beings and other animals.

questions.prompt: The kidneys are part of the ____ system.
questions.explanation: The kidneys are part of the urinary system.

questions.prompt: The kidneys filter ____ wastes from the blood and excrete them from the body.
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter nitrogenous wastes from the blood and excrete them from the body.

questions.prompt: If there is more water in the blood, the kidneys produce ____ urine.
questions.explanation: If there is more water in the blood, the kidneys produce more urine.

questions.prompt: By controlling the water-solute balance of the body, the kidneys perform ____.
questions.explanation: By controlling the water-solute balance of the body, the kidneys perform osmoregulation.

questions.prompt: Urea is removed from the body by the ____.
questions.explanation: Urea is removed from the body by the kidneys.

questions.prompt: The liver breaks down the haemoglobin of dead ____.
questions.explanation: The liver breaks down the haemoglobin of dead red blood cells.

questions.prompt: The products of haemoglobin breakdown in the liver are sent to the ____ for removal.
questions.explanation: The products of haemoglobin breakdown in the liver are sent to the kidneys for removal.

questions.prompt: The liver changes ____ to urea.
questions.explanation: The liver changes ammonia to urea.

questions.prompt: The human urinary system is also called the ____ system.
questions.explanation: The human urinary system is also called the excretory system.

questions.prompt: The urinary bladder temporarily ____ urine.
questions.explanation: The urinary bladder temporarily stores urine.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the tube that carries urine from the urinary bladder to the outside.
questions.explanation: The urethra is the tube that carries urine from the urinary bladder to the outside.

questions.prompt: The human urinary system has a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a ____.
questions.explanation: The human urinary system has a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human urinary system?
questions.explanation: The urinary system has kidneys, ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows the path of urine out of the body?
questions.explanation: Urine goes from the kidney through the ureter to the urinary bladder and leaves through the urethra.

questions.prompt: In Fig. 11.8, the depression on the concave side of the kidney is labelled the ____.
questions.explanation: In Fig. 11.8, the depression on the concave side of the kidney is labelled the hilus.

questions.prompt: The kidneys are present below the ____ in the abdominal cavity.
questions.explanation: The kidneys are present below the diaphragm in the abdominal cavity.

questions.prompt: The kidneys lie in the ____ cavity.
questions.explanation: The kidneys lie in the abdominal cavity.

questions.prompt: The kidneys lie on the sides of the ____.
questions.explanation: The kidneys lie on the sides of the vertebral column.

questions.prompt: The kidneys are attached to the ____ body wall.
questions.explanation: The kidneys are attached to the dorsal body wall.

questions.prompt: The ____ kidney is slightly lower and smaller than the left kidney.
questions.explanation: The right kidney is slightly lower and smaller than the left kidney.

questions.prompt: A kidney is ____-shaped.
questions.explanation: A kidney is bean-shaped.

questions.prompt: Each kidney is about ____ cm long.
questions.explanation: Each kidney is about 10 cm long.

questions.prompt: Each kidney is about 10 cm long, 5 cm wide and ____ cm thick.
questions.explanation: Each kidney is about 10 cm long, 5 cm wide and 4 cm thick.

questions.prompt: Kidneys receive ____% of the blood supplied to the body with each heartbeat.
questions.explanation: Kidneys receive 20% of the blood supplied to the body with each heartbeat.

questions.prompt: A kidney is enclosed in a tissue called the renal ____.
questions.explanation: A kidney is enclosed in a tissue called the renal capsule.

questions.prompt: The depression on the concave side of the kidney is called the ____.
questions.explanation: The depression on the concave side of the kidney is called the hilus.

questions.prompt: The renal ____ enters the kidney at the hilus.
questions.explanation: The renal artery enters the kidney at the hilus.

questions.prompt: The renal vein and the ____ leave the kidney at the hilus.
questions.explanation: The renal vein and the ureter leave the kidney at the hilus.

questions.prompt: The renal artery enters the kidney, and the renal vein and ureter leave it, at the ____.
questions.explanation: The renal artery enters the kidney, and the renal vein and ureter leave it, at the hilus.

questions.prompt: A longitudinal section of the kidney shows ____ regions.
questions.explanation: A longitudinal section of the kidney shows two regions.

questions.prompt: The outer region of the kidney is the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The outer region of the kidney is the renal cortex.

questions.prompt: The inner region of the kidney is the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The inner region of the kidney is the renal medulla.

questions.prompt: The cone-shaped areas in the renal medulla are called renal ____.
questions.explanation: The cone-shaped areas in the renal medulla are called renal pyramids.

questions.prompt: The base of each renal pyramid faces the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The base of each renal pyramid faces the renal cortex.

questions.prompt: The tip of each renal pyramid lies in a cavity called the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The tip of each renal pyramid lies in a cavity called the renal pelvis.

questions.prompt: The renal pyramids are found in the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The renal pyramids are found in the renal medulla.

questions.prompt: The functional units of the kidneys are called ____.
questions.explanation: The functional units of the kidneys are called nephrons.

questions.prompt: The ____ is a network of capillaries.
questions.explanation: The glomerulus is a network of capillaries.

questions.prompt: The Bowman's capsule is the ____-shaped structure around the glomerulus.
questions.explanation: The Bowman's capsule is the cup-shaped structure around the glomerulus.

questions.prompt: The nephron is the ____ unit of the kidney.
questions.explanation: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.

questions.prompt: There are more than ____ nephrons in each kidney.
questions.explanation: There are more than one million nephrons in each kidney.

questions.prompt: A nephron consists of two parts: the renal corpuscle and the renal ____.
questions.explanation: A nephron consists of two parts: the renal corpuscle and the renal tubule.

questions.prompt: The first part of the nephron is the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The first part of the nephron is the renal corpuscle.

questions.prompt: The renal corpuscle is composed of the glomerulus and the ____.
questions.explanation: The renal corpuscle is composed of the glomerulus and the Bowman's capsule.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the long tube attached to the Bowman's capsule.
questions.explanation: The renal tubule is the long tube attached to the Bowman's capsule.

questions.prompt: The renal tubule has ____ parts.
questions.explanation: The renal tubule has three parts.

questions.prompt: The first part of the renal tubule is called the ____.
questions.explanation: The first part of the renal tubule is called the proximal convoluted tubule.

questions.prompt: The middle part of the renal tubule is U-shaped and is called the ____.
questions.explanation: The middle part of the renal tubule is U-shaped and is called the Loop of Henle.

questions.prompt: The last part of the renal tubule is called the ____.
questions.explanation: The last part of the renal tubule is called the distal convoluted tubule.

questions.prompt: The Loop of Henle is ____-shaped.
questions.explanation: The Loop of Henle is U-shaped.

questions.prompt: The distal convoluted tubules of many nephrons open into a single ____.
questions.explanation: The distal convoluted tubules of many nephrons open into a single collecting duct.

questions.prompt: Many collecting ducts join together and open into the renal ____.
questions.explanation: Many collecting ducts join together and open into the renal pelvis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a part of a nephron?
questions.explanation: A nephron has a renal corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman's capsule) and a renal tubule; the ureter is outside the nephron.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows the three parts of the renal tubule, starting from the Bowman's capsule?
questions.explanation: The renal tubule has the proximal convoluted tubule first, the U-shaped Loop of Henle in the middle and the distal convoluted tubule last.

options: Proximal convoluted tubule → Loop of Henle → distal convoluted tubule
Distal convoluted tubule → Loop of Henle → proximal convoluted tubule
Proximal convoluted tubule → distal convoluted tubule → Loop of Henle
Loop of Henle → proximal convoluted tubule → distal convoluted tubule

questions.prompt: In Fig. 11.10, the proximal convoluted tubule, distal convoluted tubule and Loop of Henle together form the renal ____.
questions.explanation: In Fig. 11.10, the proximal convoluted tubule, distal convoluted tubule and Loop of Henle together form the renal tubule.

questions.prompt: The glomerulus lies inside the cup-shaped ____.
questions.explanation: The glomerulus lies inside the cup-shaped Bowman's capsule.

questions.prompt: In which structure is the blood pressure very high, so that materials are filtered out of the blood?
questions.explanation: The pressure of the blood in the glomerulus is very high, which causes pressure filtration.

questions.prompt: The main role of the kidney is ____.
questions.explanation: The main role of the kidney is urine formation.

questions.prompt: Urine formation is divided into ____ sub-processes.
questions.explanation: Urine formation is divided into three sub-processes.

questions.prompt: The first step of urine formation is called ____.
questions.explanation: The first step of urine formation is called pressure filtration.

questions.prompt: The second step of urine formation is ____.
questions.explanation: The second step of urine formation is reabsorption.

questions.prompt: The three steps of urine formation are pressure filtration, tubular secretion and ____.
questions.explanation: The three steps of urine formation are pressure filtration, tubular secretion and reabsorption.

questions.prompt: The filtered material collected in the Bowman's capsule is called the glomerular ____.
questions.explanation: The filtered material collected in the Bowman's capsule is called the glomerular filtrate.

questions.prompt: The renal artery divides into many ____.
questions.explanation: The renal artery divides into many arterioles.

questions.prompt: Each arteriole divides further into the ____ of the glomerulus.
questions.explanation: Each arteriole divides further into the capillaries of the glomerulus.

questions.prompt: When blood reaches the glomerulus, its pressure is very ____.
questions.explanation: When blood reaches the glomerulus, its pressure is very high.

questions.prompt: Due to the high pressure of blood in the glomerulus, materials are filtered into the ____.
questions.explanation: Due to the high pressure of blood in the glomerulus, materials are filtered into the Bowman's capsule.

questions.prompt: Water, salts, sugars and ____ are filtered out of the glomerulus into the Bowman's capsule.
questions.explanation: Water, salts, sugars and nitrogenous wastes are filtered out of the glomerulus into the Bowman's capsule.

questions.prompt: Filtration in the glomerulus is called pressure filtration because it takes place due to the ____ of the blood.
questions.explanation: Filtration in the glomerulus is called pressure filtration because it takes place due to the pressure of the blood.

questions.prompt: Blood cells and plasma proteins are not filtered out of the glomerulus because they are ____ in size.
questions.explanation: Blood cells and plasma proteins are not filtered out of the glomerulus because they are larger in size.

questions.prompt: Pressure filtration takes place in the ____.
questions.explanation: Pressure filtration takes place in the glomerulus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT filtered out of the glomerulus into the Bowman's capsule?
questions.explanation: Water, salts, sugars and nitrogenous wastes are filtered; blood cells and plasma proteins are too large.

questions.prompt: Why are blood cells not filtered into the Bowman's capsule?
questions.explanation: Blood cells and plasma proteins are not filtered out because they are larger in size.

options: They are destroyed by the liver

questions.prompt: Blood cells and plasma proteins stay in the ____ because they are too large to be filtered.
questions.explanation: Blood cells and plasma proteins stay in the blood because they are too large to be filtered.

questions.prompt: Which statement about glomerular filtrate is correct?
questions.explanation: The glomerular filtrate becomes urine only after reabsorption and tubular secretion in the renal tubule.

options: It is the same as urine
It still contains useful substances such as glucose
It is formed after tubular secretion
It contains blood cells and plasma proteins

questions.prompt: The glomerular filtrate moves to the next part of the nephron, the renal ____.
questions.explanation: The glomerular filtrate moves to the next part of the nephron, the renal tubule.

questions.prompt: In reabsorption, the useful constituents of the glomerular filtrate go back into the ____.
questions.explanation: In reabsorption, the useful constituents of the glomerular filtrate go back into the blood capillaries.

questions.prompt: Salts are reabsorbed from the ____.
